## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the source states that \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2, lines 1354-1375]
- [proved] Under the explicit box-Schur realization \(I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), the requested restriction \(J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow J_{1,1}\) and its descent to indecomposables are established for every \(i,j,p,c\ge1\).

## Strategy
Put \(q=i+p,\ r=j+c\), and write \(\bar s_\lambda\) for the class of \(s_\lambda\) in
\[
A_{p,c}:=\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}.
\]
Here \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\) means \(\ell(\lambda)\le r\) and \(\lambda_1\le q\). Define \(J_{p,c}\) as the source ideal generated by the interval \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}\). Then
\[
J_{p,c}=
\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar s_\lambda. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the right side contains the stated generators. It is an ideal: if
\(c_{\lambda,\nu}^{\gamma}\ne0\) in
\(s_\lambda s_\nu=\sum_\gamma c_{\lambda,\nu}^{\gamma}s_\gamma\),
then \(\lambda\subseteq\gamma\). Hence every surviving \(\gamma\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}\) still contains \(i^j\); all other terms vanish in \(A_{p,c}\). This proves (1).

Since
\[
(i+1)^{j+1}\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c},
\]
one has
\[
I_{j+c,i+p}\subseteq I_{j+1,i+1},
\]
and therefore a quotient map
\[
\pi:A_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow A_{1,1}:=\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
Basiswise, for every \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+p)^{j+c}\),
\[
\pi(\bar s_\lambda)=
\begin{cases}
\bar s_\lambda,&\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},\\
0,&\lambda\not\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}.
\end{cases} \tag{2}
\]
The second case includes precisely the domain basis classes with
\(\lambda_1>i+1\) or \(\ell(\lambda)>j+1\). In the first case,
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},
\]
so \(\bar s_\lambda\in J_{1,1}\). Conversely, every basis element of
\[
J_{1,1}=
\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}}
\mathbb Z\,\bar s_\lambda
\]
is retained by (2). Thus \(\pi(J_{p,c})=J_{1,1}\).

With \(\Lambda_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}\Lambda_d\), \(\Lambda\)-linearity gives
\[
\pi(\Lambda_+J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+\pi(J_{p,c})
=\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
Hence \(\pi|_{J_{p,c}}\) descends to the surjection
\[
J_{p,c}/\Lambda_+J_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow
J_{1,1}/\Lambda_+J_{1,1}.
\]
For \(p=c=1\), \(\pi\) is the identity; the “outside” case is empty.

## Gaps
The supplied source excerpt does not itself locate the box-Schur definition of \(I_{r,q}\). The certificate is therefore established conditional on the explicit realization of \(I_{r,q}\) stated above.
